name: One story in four chapters
what: Who you are, where you stand, what is in your hands, your plan. Each chapter ends in one obvious next step; a waypoint bar tracks where the reader is.
where: The whole screen after "Show where they stand".

name: Reach / target / likely label
what: Each college gets a label from a written rule in code, from its published admit rate and middle score range. Never from a model.
where: Chapter 2; tap a college, "How we got this".

name: This one is close, and publishers disagree
what: Every label is rerun with the score 30 points either way and the admit rate 5 points lower; a label that flips is marked. Five published rulebooks are run on the same score and any disagreement is shown.

name: Where you stand: the trail map
what: Every college's middle score band on one line, the distance to the student's score written on each bar, and a label beside it.

name: Example cases, two pools kept apart
what: Counts of admitted, not admitted and waitlisted among finished cases like this student, with n and the official admit rate beside them. The school's own cases and the public self-reported pool are never added together, and the public pool's over-count is stated.

name: Who you resemble: closer to the admitted or the not admitted
what: Per college, the distance from the student to the 7 nearest admitted and the 7 nearest not-admitted cases, over score, activities rating, major group, hooks and residency. A lean, a steady test, the parts that are close or far, and the nearest cases of each. A distance, never a percentage; the label is untouched.

name: Rings picture
what: The student at the centre, one dot per college as far out as the student is from the people admitted there. Hollow when there are too few cases; on an outer ring when it cannot be placed.

name: Map picture
what: The student in the middle, a branch per label, a node per college, and under each college its nearest kind of admitted student and its three nearest admitted cases.

name: Scatter, part bars, kinds and changes
what: A scatter of that college's cases by score and activities rating with the student as a star and the three kinds' medoids ringed; a bar per part; three kinds of admitted student found by k-medoids and named from counts; and what would bring the student closer (score, activities, a named major; never hooks, home state or GPA).

name: Essay and activity text in closeness
what: With a model key, masked essay and activity text are embedded and become two more parts of the distance, compared only where both profiles have text. Vectors stay in memory. Without a key the structured parts carry the comparison.
where: Tap a college, "Who you resemble", with the working shown.

name: Activities rating input
what: A 0 to 10 dial for the counselor's own rating of the student's activities, used only by closeness.

name: What the college says it weighs
what: Statements from each college's own Common Data Set form, each with its field, year and source link, checked in code and confirmed against a knowledge base. Common beliefs are checked against the form.
where: Tap a college, "What the college says".

name: What the college looks for, beside the profile
what: For each factor the college says it reads, whether it is in this profile, not yet, or cannot be seen here. Three neutral states and no total: it is not a score.

name: List balance and suggested fills
what: Warnings when a list is reach-heavy, has no likely or no target, piles onto very selective colleges, or is short. Suggested colleges that would be likely or target, preferring the home state.

name: "What if the score were…" slider
what: Moves the student's score and re-labels the whole list as it moves, saying which colleges change at which score. Labels only; nothing else is re-run.

name: Cost: sticker price and what families paid
what: The published sticker cost beside the federal average paid after grants, by income band when given. One family's price can differ, and the screen says so.

name: Your plan, and a sheet to print
what: Five things to do this month from the list and its gaps, and a one-page print layout for the family in plain words.

name: Keep track, and pay it forward
what: A status for each college (considering, applying, submitted, result). When a result comes in it becomes a finished case for next year's students, with no names.

name: Essay notes with quotes, after masking
what: Names, addresses, phones and dates are masked, then one model reads the essay and returns observations with word-for-word quotes; code drops any note whose quote is not in the essay. A second model tags the major independently. An essay with instructions aimed at an AI is stopped twice.

name: Show the working
what: One switch reveals every source, rule, check and step behind the screen: the five steps, what code did and what a model did, sentences hidden by checks, the privacy record, and the closeness check table.

name: About, and How we worked this out
what: A tour with live buttons; the parts and weights, the algorithm as a diagram, the libraries, the choices made, every data source with what was taken from it, and this feature list. Weights and thresholds are read from the engine, not typed into the page.
where: "About" in the header; Counselor tools, "How we worked this out".

name: Add a finished case
what: A counselor records a finished case for the school's own pool. Anything that looks like a name, email, phone or date of birth is refused.

name: No personal chance of admission
what: The screen never shows a percentage for the student. Asking why gets the measured over-count of the public pool and a pointer to the evidence instead.
where: "Why there is no percentage" in chapter 2; every count sits beside the official admit rate.

name: Holds-up check for closeness
what: 400 past posters, each hidden in turn, their lean computed and their real outcome counted. Shown as counts with the caveat about self-reporting.

name: Applicant-evidence package
what: A store for applicant records with provenance and consent, intake from messy files, and a weighted similarity score that reports how much of a profile could be compared. Its scorer orders the example cases.

name: 1,339 colleges from the federal file
what: The full Scorecard institution file with cost and net price, and a "did you mean" for a college typed slightly wrong.

name: Shared preview with no server
what: Saved runs for the demo students, with the what-if scores, as plain files that open from a folder or a zip.

name: Tests and the acceptance sheet
what: Automated tests with no network, including one that fails if the fixture or this feature list drifts from its copies. 60 labels worked out by hand from the published rows, separately from the label code: 60 of 60 match.
where: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ; python tests/acceptance/run_acceptance.py

name: Parser for raw public posts
what: Turns raw r/collegeresults posts into a wider pool (654 colleges in our run). Not wired in; its output stays out of the repository because it holds snippets of people's posts.

name: PRISM Evaluator on the essay notes
what: The run's score is read back in code instead.

name: Several intended majors in the form
what: Closeness can try another major the student named, but the form sends only one; the API accepts major_interests.

name: Essay baseline search and activity text comparison
what: A student draft searches a standalone reference bank using embeddings when available and local text similarity otherwise. Undergraduate samples are original synthetic essays; licensed graduate references come from OpenEssays with attribution. Missing applicant essay text is omitted from outcome comparisons.
where: Essay search in the header; input and similar references displayed side by side.
